question: In the context of Five Year Plans, what does the term "plan holiday" refer to?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Discontinuity in five-year planning**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

 
 
• The term **"Plan Holiday"** refers to the period when the government temporarily halts the implementation of Five-Year Plans. This term is associated with a break in the sequence of planning and the adoption of annual plans instead of a long-term Five-Year Plan. 
 
• In India, the concept of a "Plan Holiday" was introduced after the third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966). This break occurred due to the economic and political challenges faced by the country, particularly the **Indo-China War of 1962**, the **Indo-Pak War of 1965**, and the **severe droughts of the mid-1960s**. 
 
• During the Plan Holiday (1966-1969), the government implemented three **Annual Plans** instead of launching a new Five-Year Plan. These were short-term plans aimed at stabilizing the economy and addressing immediate challenges.
